chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Walking in a rush will destroy a believer’s dignity.
ai.seo_question: What effect does hurried walking have on a believer's dignity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), linking physical demeanor to spiritual status by noting that hurried walking erodes the believer's 'bahā' (splendor or dignity). This reflects the Shia emphasis on 'hayā' (modesty) and 'wajr' (dignity) as outward manifestations of inner faith, where composure signifies self-control and reverence for one's spiritual station.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-30 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor al-Vaseti, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid that Abil Hassan Al-Kadhim (MGB) said, “
Walking in a rush will destroy a believer’s dignity.”
